Ongoing reforms to improve the level and quality of training in Kenya’s civil service include a shift toward competency-based human resource development and capacity building. The Public Service Commission’s Competency Framework is intended to move the public service away from relying mainly on academic qualifications, seniority and oral interviews, and toward demonstrated competencies, practical/written testing, capacity assessment, competency testing, performance management and promotion based on possession of required competencies. This framework is meant to guide recruitment, placement, career development, performance measurement and staff development, thereby linking training more directly to skills gaps and service-delivery results.

Another major reform is the strengthening of the Kenya School of Government. Under the Kenya School of Government Act, KSG is mandated to build civil service capacity through specialized and targeted training, induction programmes, consultancy and research services. Earlier reform plans also allocated funds to upgrade KSG facilities and strengthen faculty capacity, with the aim of improving the quality of training offered to public officers.

The government has also used broader capacity-building frameworks, including the National Capacity Building Framework and public sector reform plans under Vision 2030 Medium Term Plans, to strengthen administrative capacity, support devolution, improve coordination between national and county governments, and enhance public service delivery. In addition, the Capacity Assessment and Rationalization of the Public Service reform was designed to address human resource management challenges in a harmonized way, improve effectiveness and efficiency, and reduce duplication of roles. Overall, the reforms focus on modernizing HRM, making training more targeted and competency-based, strengthening public service training institutions, and linking training to performance, ethics, leadership and service delivery.
answers.r: The sources directly mention capacity building and training reforms, the Kenya School of Government’s mandate for specialized and targeted training and induction, the National Capacity Building Framework, and the Competency Framework’s role in capacity assessment, competency testing, career development and performance management. These measures are relevant to improving both the level and quality of civil service training.
